content.title: National Law Enforcement Week
content.summary: National Police Week, established in 1962, is observed every May with events honoring fallen law enforcement officers, including a Candlelight Vigil at the National Law Enforcement Memorial and Museum in Washington D.C. The city of Arvada remembers its fallen officers, including W. Michael Northey, Robert Beghtol, Gordon Beesley, and Dillon Vakoff, with memorials and named facilities in their honor.
content.body:
## Annual Tribute to Fallen Heroes

National Police Week occurs every May and is commemorated with live, in-person events. The National Law Enforcement Memorial and Museum in Washington D.C. holds ceremonies, including the Annual Candlelight Vigil, to honor the fallen officers whose names have recently been added to the Memorial.

National Law Enforcement Week was established in 1962. Events across the country honor those who paid the ultimate sacrifice.

### Arvada Fallen Officers

- **W. Michael Northey**

  - [Officer Northey](https://www.arvadaco.gov/581/Officer-W-Michael-Northey) was killed after being struck by a car while making an arrest in 1979. Shortly after his death, the Michael Northey Park, located at 11364 W 84th Ave, was named in his honor.
- **Robert Beghtol**

  - [Officer Beghtol](/578/Officer-Robert-G-Beghtol) died in 1961 during Scuba Diving Unit practice at the lake near 60th and Tennyson. The Arvada Police training facility, the Beghtol Building, is named in his honor.
- **Gordon Beesley**

  - Officer [Gordon Beesley](/576/Officer-Gordon-Beesley) was shot in the line of duty on June 21, 2021.
- **Dillon Vakoff**

  - Officer [Dillon Vakoff](/582/Officer-Dillon-Vakoff) was killed in the line of duty on September 11, 2022**.**
